leads.title: Lake and marsh reclamation by dikes and windmills in the Low Countries
leads.date: wind drainage from 1408; lakes drained 1533 to 1612
leads.why: A large part of the Netherlands was made this way, and Dutch engineers carried the methods to the English Fens, France, the Baltic and beyond.
leads.verify: First dated wind-driven drainage mills (Alkmaar, 1408), the first drained lakes (Achtermeer, 1533) and the Beemster (1612); the water boards as the institution that ran them. Diked polder fields in the Yangtze delta from the Tang and Song periods are an earlier separate origin.

leads.title: Feedback control engineering in the United States
leads.where: New York, Massachusetts and New Jersey
leads.why: Three-term controllers and servomechanisms came to run chemical plants, power grids, aircraft, weapons and factory machines.
leads.verify: The dated contributions and how they connect: Minorsky's 1922 analysis of ship steering, Black's negative-feedback amplifier (1927), Nyquist's stability criterion (1932), Hazen's servomechanism theory (1934) and the first commercial proportional-integral-derivative process controllers (1930s). Its roots are the windmill and steam-engine governor and Maxwell's 1868 paper; parallel work in Germany and the Soviet Union should be noted.

leads.title: Spear-thrower (woomera) in Aboriginal Australia
leads.where: Australia, with early depictions in Arnhem Land and the Kimberley
leads.date: by the mid-Holocene, perhaps c. 4000 BCE or earlier (dating contested)
leads.why: The woomera became the main hunting weapon across most of the continent and doubled as a dish, fire saw and chisel handle.
leads.verify: The earliest dated evidence for spear-throwers in Australia (rock-art sequences in Arnhem Land, any direct finds, skeletal indicators) and what archaeologists conclude about whether it was invented in Australia or arrived with earlier people. Dating is weak; give the range and the basis.

leads.title: Serial shipbuilding at the Venetian Arsenal
leads.why: A state yard that built and fitted out galleys from stocked standard parts along a set route showed Europe what organised large-scale production could do.
leads.verify: When the Arsenal began to build to standard designs with stockpiled parts and staged fitting-out (the expansions of 1320 and after; the fleets of the sixteenth century), and how much of the famous 'assembly line' is later exaggeration. Earlier state shipyards elsewhere are worth a note.

leads.title: Water-powered fulling and hammer mills in medieval Europe
leads.why: The camshaft turned the grain mill into a general industrial engine for cloth, iron, paper, tanning and ore, on which Europe's later mechanisation was built.
leads.verify: The earliest reliable documents for fulling mills and forge hammers (tenth and eleventh century Italy and France) and for hemp, tanning and paper mills. State what is known about continuity from Roman ore-stamping mills, reinvention, or transmission from the Islamic world or China; the evidence does not settle it.

leads.title: Cranes with winch and pulley in Archaic Greece
leads.where: Corinth, Athens and the Aegean, Greece
leads.why: Small teams could now raise building stone without ramps, and the compound pulley, treadwheel crane and harbour crane all followed.
leads.verify: The archaeological argument for the date (lifting-tong and lewis cuttings on temple blocks), the recent case for simpler lifting frames at Corinth and Isthmia in the seventh century BCE, and the earliest evidence for the pulley itself (Assyrian reliefs).

concepts.name: Automatic control engineering
concepts.summary: Designing self-correcting machines and processes by analysing feedback, using controllers that act on the measured error.

concepts.name: Cam-operated powered hammers
concepts.summary: Using lugs or cams on a turning shaft to lift and drop hammers, so that rotary power does pounding work.

concepts.name: Crane
concepts.summary: Lifting and placing heavy loads with a rope run over pulleys from a winch on a raised frame.

concepts.name: Polder reclamation
concepts.summary: Winning farmland from marsh, lake or sea by enclosing it with dikes and pumping the water out.

concepts.name: Spear-thrower
concepts.summary: A hand-held lever that launches a separate dart or spear, found among many separate peoples such as the Australian woomera and the American atlatl.

concepts.name: Standardised serial production
concepts.summary: Making large numbers of near-identical goods to a set pattern in supervised workshops with divided tasks and checks on quality.
